title: selinum cicutarium
intro: Selinum cicutarium, commonly known as wild hemlock or poison parsley, is a plant species in the carrot family that is native to Europe and Asia. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifungal properties, which may help to alleviate symptoms of colds, flu, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Selinum cicutarium include its ability to stimulate digestion, relieve flatulence, and reduce fever, making it a popular remedy in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
